final_message:
The oracle provider now emits one `FixedIn` entry per (version, architecture), with an `Arch` key, only when the architecture changes the fix. All 911 unit tests pass. I also ran the full suite earlier and its only other failures were 15 tests in `tests/quality/test_configure.py`, which fail because `yardstick` isn't installed. I didn't re-run that directory after my last changes.

- **When `Arch` is set:** a version that doesn't ship for every architecture in the advisory gets one entry per architecture it ships for. ELSA-2022-4803 now gives rsyslog `…57.0.4…` for aarch64 and `…57.0.1…` for x86_64.
- **When `Arch` is left out:** if a version ships for every architecture, it gets a single entry with no `Arch` key. That covers a fix shared by all architectures and several rebuilds that each ship everywhere.
- **Mixed case:** if one rebuild ships everywhere and another only on one architecture, the first is arch-less and the second carries `Arch`. That was my reading of the rules; say so if you want it handled differently.
- **Parser:** the OVAL parser previously flattened the criteria tree and discarded the "Oracle Linux arch is X" criterion. It now keeps it with the packages beneath it, in `oval_parser.py`. The regex for it is in `parser.py`. The collapsing into `FixedIn` entries happens in `_collapse_arches`, and output is now sorted so it's deterministic.
- **Schema:** I added `schema/vulnerability/os/schema-1.1.1.json`, which is 1.1.0 plus an optional `FixedIn.Arch` string. Only oracle uses it, through a new `OS_SCHEMA_VERSION_WITH_ARCH` constant in `schema.py`. The default `OS_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays at 1.1.0, so other providers are unchanged.
- **Tests:** I added a `mock_arch_data` fixture and `test_parse_arch_specific_fixes`, covering the arch-specific, all-architecture-rebuilds and shared-fix cases. The two oracle snapshots changed only in their schema URL, now 1.1.1.
- **`answer.json`:** written in the repo root with the one-sentence summary.

python3 - <<'EOF'
hdr=open('test-fixtures/mock_ksplice_data').read().split('<definitions>')[0]
def crit(arch, pkgs):
    out=f'<criteria operator="AND">\n<criterion test_ref="t:{arch}" comment="Oracle Linux arch is {arch}"/>\n<criteria operator="OR">\n'
    for i,(p,v) in enumerate(pkgs):
        out+=f'<criteria operator="AND">\n<criterion test_ref="t:{arch}{i}" comment="{p} is earlier than {v}"/>\n<criterion test_ref="t:s{i}" comment="{p} is signed with the Oracle Linux 7 key"/>\n</criteria>\n'
    return out+'</criteria>\n</criteria>\n'
def d(n,title,body):
    return f'''<definition id="oval:com.oracle.elsa:def:{n}" version="501" class="patch">
<metadata>
<title> ELSA-{title}: rsyslog security update (MODERATE) </title>
<affected family="unix">
<platform>Oracle Linux 7</platform>
</affected>
<reference source="elsa" ref_id="ELSA-{title}" ref_url="https://linux.oracle.com/errata/ELSA-{title}.html"/>
<description> test </description>
<advisory>
<severity>MODERATE</severity>
<issued date="2022-06-01"/>
</advisory>
</metadata>
<criteria operator="AND">
<criterion test_ref="t:ol" comment="Oracle Linux 7 is installed"/>
<criteria operator="OR">
{body}</criteria>
</criteria>
</definition>
'''
x=d(1,"2022-4803",crit("aarch64",[("rsyslog","0:8.24.0-57.0.4.el7_9.3")])+crit("x86_64",[("rsyslog","0:8.24.0-57.0.1.el7_9.3")]))
y=d(2,"2022-4804",crit("aarch64",[("rsyslog","0:8.24.0-57.0.1.el7_9.3"),("rsyslog","0:8.24.0-57.0.2.el7_9.3")])+crit("x86_64",[("rsyslog","0:8.24.0-57.0.1.el7_9.3"),("rsyslog","0:8.24.0-57.0.2.el7_9.3")]))
z=d(3,"2022-4805",crit("aarch64",[("rsyslog","0:8.24.0-57.el7_9.3")])+crit("x86_64",[("rsyslog","0:8.24.0-57.el7_9.3")]))
open('test-fixtures/mock_arch_data','w').write(hdr+'<definitions>\n'+x+y+z+'</definitions>\n</oval_definitions>\n')
EOF
cat >> test_oracle.py <<'EOF'


def test_parse_arch_specific_fixes(tmpdir, helpers):
    subject = parser.Parser(workspace=workspace.Workspace(tmpdir, "test", create=True))
    vuln_dict = subject._parse_oval_data(helpers.local_dir("test-fixtures/mock_arch_data"), subject.config)

    def fixes(vuln_id):
        _, record = vuln_dict[(vuln_id, "ol:7")]
        return {(f["Version"], f.get("Arch")) for f in record["Vulnerability"]["FixedIn"]}, len(
            record["Vulnerability"]["FixedIn"]
        )

    # the architecture differentiates the fix
    assert fixes("ELSA-2022-4803") == (
        {("0:8.24.0-57.0.4.el7_9.3", "aarch64"), ("0:8.24.0-57.0.1.el7_9.3", "x86_64")},
        2,
    )
    # several rebuilds, each shipped for every architecture
    assert fixes("ELSA-2022-4804") == (
        {("0:8.24.0-57.0.1.el7_9.3", None), ("0:8.24.0-57.0.2.el7_9.3", None)},
        2,
    )
    # a single fix shared by every architecture
    assert fixes("ELSA-2022-4805") == ({("0:8.24.0-57.el7_9.3", None)}, 1)
EOF
cd ../../../..; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/unit 2>&1 | tail -3
echo '{"summary": "The oracle provider now emits per-architecture FixedIn entries (with an Arch key) only when the fix version differs by architecture, and arch-less entries otherwise, and advertises the new OS schema 1.1.1 while other providers stay on 1.1.0."}' > answer.json
